symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Number of independent observations of all supplied pairs.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: Fixed Holder smoothness index of the one-dimensional mechanisms and log densities.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Fixed radius for the smoothness envelope.

symbols.name: sigmaK
symbols.def: Fixed bandwidth used by every Gaussian kernel.

symbols.name: ghi
symbols.def: Fixed upper GENE correcting-gain margin with \(\underline g<\overline g\).

symbols.name: AH
symbols.def: Fixed width factor for the local residual-HSIC window.

symbols.name: lambda0
symbols.def: \(\lambda_0\) is the local signal radius certified by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:attainable\text{-}margin\text{-}rectangle}\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X=(X_j:j\in I)\), the first labelled coordinate of each supplied pair.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(Y=(Y_j:j\in I)\), the second labelled coordinate of each supplied pair.

symbols.name: Sample
symbols.def: \(\mathcal W_n=(W_1,\ldots,W_n)\) is an independent sample from \(P\).

symbols.name: f
symbols.def: Structural regression functions for the true directions.

symbols.name: muK
symbols.def: Mean embedding of a law \(R\) into \(\mathcal H_{k\otimes\ell}\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: \(H=(H_{j,b}:(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d)\) denotes fixed-kernel population residual HSIC.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: \(q=(q_{j,b}:(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d)\) denotes the scale-normalized explained variance.

symbols.name: score
symbols.def: \(s=(s_{j,b}:(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d)\) denotes the pairwise population GENE order scores.

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: \(g=(g_j:j\in I)\) denotes the population GENE correcting gains.

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: Joint map collecting GENE gains and every query-indexed residual HSIC value.

symbols.name: PiTheta
symbols.def: \(\Pi_\theta((u_j)_{j\in I},(v_{j,+})_{j\in I},(v_{j,-})_{j\in I})=((u_j)_{j\in I},(v_{j,\theta_j})_{j\in I},(v_{j,-\theta_j})_{j\in I})\); thus each ordered block \((H_{j,+},H_{j,-})\) is sent to \((H_{j,\theta_j},H_{j,-\theta_j})\).

symbols.name: Fd
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak F_d\), the feasible image of the joint population margin map.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: \(a=(a_j:j\in I)\), the standardized Gaussian correlation coordinate.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: \(t=(t_j:j\in I)\), the nonlinear Hermite perturbation coordinate.

symbols.name: tpath
symbols.def: For \(j\in I\), \(t^{[j]}(u)_j=u\) and \(t^{[j]}(u)_k=0\) for every \(k\ne j\); all coordinates other than the scalar \(j\)-coordinate are fixed along the path.

symbols.name: phi
symbols.def: \(\phi(z)=z^2-1\), the second centered Gaussian Hermite polynomial.

symbols.name: kappaH
symbols.def: For \(v\in(0,1)\), fix any \(j\in I\), orientation \(\theta\), and \(a\) with \(a_j=v\), and set \(\kappa_H(v)=\lim_{u\downarrow0}u^{-2}H_{j,-\theta_j}(P_{a,t^{[j]}(u),\theta})\). Along \(t^{[j]}(u)\), every coordinate other than \(j\) is fixed at zero; factorization of \(P_{a,t,\theta}\) makes the displayed coordinate functional independent of the remaining entries of \(a\).

symbols.name: Folds
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_n=(I_1,I_2,I_3,I_4)\) is the deterministic balanced four-fold partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) by observation index, with fold sizes differing by at most one.

symbols.name: Afit
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), the admissible foldwise local-polynomial regression class fixed by Definition \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: RegEvent
symbols.def: The simultaneous foldwise \(L^4\) regression-accuracy event in Definition \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}good\text{-}event}\).

symbols.name: OrthHandle
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{orth}}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}})\), the second-order residual-embedding orthogonalization route applied only to the admissible four-fold local-polynomial class.

symbols.name: Tperp
symbols.def: \((\widehat H^{\perp}_{j,b}(\widehat m):(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d)\), to be derived from \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{orth}}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}})\) for \(\widehat m\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\).

symbols.name: Bset
symbols.def: \((B_j:j\in I)\), the pairwise acceptance sets formed by simultaneous inversion.

symbols.name: Chat
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n\), the simultaneous orientation confidence set.

symbols.name: Nstar
symbols.def: \(N^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)\), the smallest sample size allowing worst-case exact-orientation error at most \(\alpha\) over \(\mathcal M_d(\lambda)\).

assumptions.condition: \[(f_j,p^C_j,p^\varepsilon_j)\text{ satisfies Peters et al.'s Condition 19 for every }j\in I.\]

novel.justification: The fixed weighted Holder envelope describes smooth mechanisms and smooth log densities on unbounded supports in one common scale. It contains Gaussian causes and noises together with bounded smooth log-density perturbations and polynomially growing nonlinear mechanisms, covering standardized physical measurement pairs whose response curve is smooth and whose tails remain Gaussian-like.

assumptions.condition: \[c_0e^{-C_0z^2}\le p_j(z)\le C_0e^{-c_0z^2}\quad\text{for every }p_j\in\{p^C_j,p^\varepsilon_j\},\ z\in\mathbb R,\ j\in I.\]

novel.justification: The two-sided density envelope retains full support while excluding tail sequences that become arbitrarily sparse. It is satisfied by standardized Gaussian causes and noises and by uniformly bounded smooth exponential tilts of them, a concrete domain for continuously measured pairs with approximately Gaussian latent shocks.

The navigation window selects supplied pairs with stable, nondegenerate GENE correcting gains. Moderate-signal systems in which the true mechanism explains an interior fraction of effect variance satisfy this restriction, including the oriented Hermite chart over any compact interior correlation interval.

The residual-HSIC window defines a local batch of pairs whose wrong-direction departures from independence have comparable strength within a fixed factor. Such batches arise when scientific modules are screened to a common detection scale, and the Hermite chart realizes every coordinate of this window while preserving positive densities and restricted-ANM identification.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_d(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_d(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)=\{(P,\theta,f,p^C,p^\varepsilon):d\ge1\text{ and the eight member properties listed below hold}\}.\]

definitions.name: orientation-indexed HSIC-block permutation
definitions.construction: \[\Pi_\theta\bigl((u_j)_{j\in I},(v_{j,+})_{j\in I},(v_{j,-})_{j\in I}\bigr)=\bigl((u_j)_{j\in I},(v_{j,\theta_j})_{j\in I},(v_{j,-\theta_j})_{j\in I}\bigr).\]

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_d(\lambda)\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_d(\lambda)=\{(P,\theta,f,p^C,p^\varepsilon)\in\mathcal M_d(\beta,L,c_0,C_0):\underline g\le g_j\le\overline g,\ \lambda\le H_{j,-\theta_j}\le A_H\lambda\text{ for every }j\in I\}.\]

definitions.name: one-coordinate Hermite path
definitions.construction: \[t^{[j]}(u)_k=u\mathbf 1\{k=j\},\qquad u\ge0,\quad j,k\in I.\] Thus coordinate \(j\) varies with the scalar \(u\), while every other coordinate remains fixed at zero.

definitions.name: oriented Hermite perturbation chart
definitions.construction: For \(a_j\in(0,1)\) and \(0\le t_j<\sqrt{(1-a_j^2)/2}\), draw independent \(Z_j,\xi_j\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), set \(F_{a_j,t_j}(z)=a_jz+t_j\phi(z)\) and \(s_{a_j,t_j}=\sqrt{1-a_j^2-2t_j^2}\), and define \((X_j,Y_j)=(Z_j,F_{a_j,t_j}(Z_j)+s_{a_j,t_j}\xi_j)\) when \(\theta_j=+1\) and the coordinate-swapped pair when \(\theta_j=-1\); \(P_{a,t,\theta}=\bigotimes_{j\in I}\mathcal L(X_j,Y_j)\). Boundary values with \(t_k=0\) are included in the chart domain to define scalar-coordinate limits.

definitions.name: balanced cyclic four-fold allocation
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal I_{n,r}=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:i\equiv r\pmod 4\}\), with residues relabelled as \(r\in\{1,2,3,4\}\). For rotation \(r\), folds \((\mathcal I_{n,r},\mathcal I_{n,r+1},\mathcal I_{n,r+2},\mathcal I_{n,r+3})\), with indices read modulo four, are assigned respectively to regression fitting, derivative-projection fitting, the first corrected-feature mean, and the second corrected-feature mean; the four rotation-specific statistics are averaged.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}=\left\{\widehat m=(\widehat m^{(r)}_{j,b}:r\in\{1,2,3,4\},(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d):\widehat m\text{ is produced by the following deterministic protocol}\right\}.\] On regression fold \(\mathcal I_{n,r}\), for \(x\in\mathbb R\), set \(z=\pi_{T_n}(x)\) and let \((\widehat a_0,\ldots,\widehat a_{p_{\mathrm{LP}}})\) be the unique minimizer of \[\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{n,r}:\,|C_{j,b}(W_i)|\le T_n}K_{z,n}\!\left(\frac{C_{j,b}(W_i)-z}{h_n}\right)\left[E_{j,b}(W_i)-\sum_{q=0}^{p_{\mathrm{LP}}}a_q(C_{j,b}(W_i)-z)^q\right]^2+n^{-2}\sum_{q=0}^{p_{\mathrm{LP}}}a_q^2.\] Here \(K_{z,n}(v)=K_{\mathrm{LP}}(v)\) for \(|z|\le T_n-h_n\), \(K_{z,n}(v)=2K_{\mathrm{LP}}(v)\mathbf 1\{v\ge0\}\) for \(z<-T_n+h_n\), and \(K_{z,n}(v)=2K_{\mathrm{LP}}(v)\mathbf 1\{v\le0\}\) for \(z>T_n-h_n\). Set \(\widehat m^{(r)}_{j,b}(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B_n,B_n]}(\widehat a_0)\). The ridge makes the minimizer unique, so the displayed set is a nonempty singleton collection of all four rotation-specific fits; no other nuisance fit is admissible.

definitions.name: simultaneous admissible-regression event
definitions.construction: For \(x\ge1\), \(u=x+\log(2d)\), \(C_m>0\), and \(\widehat m\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), define \[\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)=\left\{\max_{r\in\{1,2,3,4\}}\max_{(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d}\|\widehat m^{(r)}_{j,b}-m_{j,b}\|_{L^4(P_{C_{j,b}})}\le C_m\left(r_n+\sqrt{\frac{u}{n}}\right)\right\}.\]

definitions.name: second-order residual-embedding orthogonalization handle
definitions.construction: For each \(\widehat m\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) and each cyclic rotation of \(\mathcal I_n\), form generated residuals from the designated regression fold, project the first Gateaux derivative of the centered Gaussian-kernel residual feature map on the conditional-mean tangent using only the designated derivative-projection fold, form two corrected feature means on the two remaining folds, cross-multiply them, remove the estimated second-order diagonal term using the derivative-projection fold, studentize with held-out conditional variances, and average the four rotation-specific statistics. The construction must be measurable in the four allocated folds and is evaluated on \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\).

definitions.name: simultaneous orientation rule and confidence set
definitions.construction: Fix the unique \(\widehat m\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\). With \(x_\alpha=\log(8/\alpha)\) and the corresponding simultaneous threshold \(u_{d,\alpha}=x_\alpha+\log(2d)\), use the four-rotation cross-fitted squared-risk estimates for \(q_{j,b}\) and the intervals delivered by \(\widehat H^\perp_{j,b}(\widehat m)\) for all \((j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d\). Let \(B_j\subseteq\{-1,+1\}\) contain \(b\) exactly when its residual-HSIC interval contains \(0\), the interval for \(-b\) intersects \([\lambda,\infty)\), and the lower confidence bound for \(s_{j,b}-s_{j,-b}\) is nonnegative; replace an empty \(B_j\) by \(\{-1,+1\}\). Set \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n=\prod_{j\in I}B_j\), and let \(\widehat\theta_n\) be its unique element when it is a singleton and a fixed measurable element otherwise.

statements.statement: For every \((P,\theta,f,p^C,p^\varepsilon)\in\mathcal M_d(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\), \(H_{j,\theta_j}=0\) for all \(j\in I\). If the mechanism is non-affine, Peters et al.'s restricted-ANM condition rules out the reverse additive-noise representation, so characteristic Gaussian kernels give \(H_{j,-\theta_j}>0\), and \(\theta_j\) is the unique population direction with zero residual HSIC.
statements.justification: This separates qualitative direction identification from the quantitative margins used by the statistical frontier.
statements.gap: Peters et al. (2014, Definition 27 and Theorem 28) establish uniqueness, while Mooij et al. (2016, Appendix A) use this residual asymmetry for pointwise consistency; neither result quantifies the joint GENE--HSIC image.
statements.consumer: Every later orientation rule can use the deterministic \(2d\)-query universe without enumerating causal orders.

statements.statement: There exist fixed \(0<a_-<a_+<1\), \(t_0>0\), \(0<\underline g<\overline g<1\), \(A_H>1\), \(\lambda_0>0\), and an envelope \((\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\) such that, for every fixed \(\theta\in\{-1,+1\}^I\), each chart law \(P_{a,t,\theta}\) with \(a\in[a_-,a_+]^d\) and \(0<t_j\le t_0\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_d(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\). For each \(j\), the scalar-coordinate path \(u\mapsto P_{a,t^{[j]}(u),\theta}\), with every coordinate \(k\ne j\) fixed at zero, satisfies uniformly in \(a_j\) \[H_{j,-\theta_j}(P_{a,t^{[j]}(u),\theta})=\kappa_H(a_j)u^2+O(u^3),\qquad g_j(P_{a,t^{[j]}(u),\theta},\theta)=\frac{a_j^2}{2}+O(u^2),\] where \(\kappa_H(a_j)=\lim_{u\downarrow0}u^{-2}H_{j,-\theta_j}(P_{a,t^{[j]}(u),\theta})\), \(\inf_{v\in[a_-,a_+]}\kappa_H(v)>0\), and the one-sided Jacobian of the full positive chart coordinate \((a_j,t_j^2)\mapsto(g_j,H_{j,-\theta_j})\) has determinant bounded away from zero. Consequently, for every \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), \[[\underline g,\overline g]^d\times\{0\}^d\times[\lambda,A_H\lambda]^d\subseteq\left\{\Pi_\theta\bigl(\Gamma_d(P_{a,t,\theta},\theta)\bigr):a\in[a_-,a_+]^d,\ 0<t_j\le t_0\text{ for every }j\in I\right\}\subseteq\Pi_\theta(\mathfrak F_d).\]
statements.justification: This unconditional feasible-image theorem and its orientation-indexed coordinate placement are the field headline: the minimax margins are populated by legal positive-density ANMs rather than imposed coordinatewise.
statements.gap: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6) and Theorem 4.3) assume favorable score ordering, and Peters et al. (2014) prove only qualitative identification; neither gives a local box theorem for their coupled population functionals.
statements.consumer: Uniform lower and upper bounds can be stated over one nonempty causal class, and benchmark designers can tune signal strength without leaving that class.

statements.statement: For the one-pair chart with \(t^2\asymp\lambda\), let \(P^+_{a,t}\) and \(P^-_{a,t}\) be the two coordinate-swapped orientation laws. Uniformly for \(a\in[a_-,a_+]\), both laws lie in \(\mathcal M_1(\lambda)\), and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) satisfy \[c\lambda\le h^2(P^+_{a,t},P^-_{a,t})\le \operatorname{KL}(P^+_{a,t}\|P^-_{a,t})\le C\lambda.\] The score expansions and density-ratio expansion are uniform under the same fixed envelope.
statements.justification: The mirror calculation links the causal margin \(\lambda\) to one-sample testing information without introducing an unrelated divergence assumption.
statements.gap: Acharya et al. (2023, Theorems 1.1--1.5) derive intervention--observation tradeoffs for discrete causal-structure identification, and Jin (2026, arXiv:2608.15840v1, Theorem 3.1) derives a bivariate linear-LiNGAM frontier from edge, non-Gaussianity, and scale margins; neither constructs opposite-orientation nonlinear restricted-ANM laws whose fixed-kernel residual-HSIC margin and testing information are both of order \(\lambda\).
statements.consumer: The proposition is the legal one-coordinate experiment needed for the product-testing converse.

statements.statement: There are universal constants \(c_1,c_2>0\) such that, for all \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), and \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), every measurable estimator \(\widetilde\theta\) satisfies \[n\le c_1\frac{\log((d+1)/\alpha)}{\lambda}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\sup_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d(\lambda)}P^{\otimes n}(\widetilde\theta\ne\theta)>\alpha.\] Moreover, any random set \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}\subseteq\{-1,+1\}^I\) with uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) obeys \[\sup_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d(\lambda)}P^{\otimes n}(|\widetilde{\mathcal C}|>1)\ge c_2\] in the same subcritical regime after a universal adjustment of \(c_1\).
statements.justification: This supplies the all-procedure necessity of both the confidence and dimension logarithms under exact simultaneous loss.
statements.gap: Existing minimax HSIC results treat one observed-variable independence problem. Acharya et al. (2023) use interventions and a discrete total-variation causal-structure margin, while Jin (2026, Theorem 3.1) uses bivariate linear LiNGAM primitive margins; none gives the \(\log d\) exact-recovery lower bound through legal nonlinear residual-HSIC product mirrors.
statements.consumer: No causal-discovery algorithm can claim a uniformly earlier singleton transition on the stated supplied-pair experiment.

statements.statement: Can the second-order residual-embedding orthogonalization handle construct, for every \(\widehat m\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), measurable statistics \((\widehat H^\perp_{j,b}(\widehat m):(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d)\) and data-dependent radii for which there are constants \(c_u,C_H,C_R,C_m>0\), depending only on the fixed envelope and kernels, such that uniformly over \(\mathcal M_d(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\), every \(x\ge1\) with \(u=x+\log(2d)\le c_u n\) satisfies \[P^{\otimes n}\!\left(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)^c\ \cup\ \left\{\exists(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d:\ |\widehat H^\perp_{j,b}(\widehat m)-H_{j,b}|>C_H\left(\sqrt{\frac{H_{j,b}u}{n}}+\frac{u}{n}+r_n^4\right)\right\}\right)\le2e^{-x}.\] On \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\), the construction must cancel the first Gateaux derivative and the second-order diagonal bias and bound the remaining nuisance term by \[C_H\max_{r,j,b}\|\widehat m^{(r)}_{j,b}-m_{j,b}\|_{L^4(P_{C_{j,b}})}^4\le C_R\left(r_n^4+\frac{u^2}{n^2}\right),\] with \(u^2/n^2\) absorbed by the displayed \(u/n\) term. The associated null intervals must use this same \(u\)-threshold and attain joint coverage. The quantifier ranges only over \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\); no unspecified regression learner is permitted. Does such a jointly valid construction exist under this fixed protocol?
statements.justification: This is the exposed uniform-nuisance kill test for one fully specified estimator class: it must establish the simultaneous \(L^4\) regression event and consume that guarantee through a fourth-order residual-embedding remainder.
statements.gap: Hl\'avka, Hu\v{s}kov\'a, and Meintanis (2011) derive nuisance-aware asymptotics, Mooij et al. (2016) prove pointwise consistency for a suitable learner, and Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (2023) observe the tested variables; none proves the joint high-probability regression and orthogonal-HSIC expansion for the fixed four-fold local-polynomial protocol.
statements.consumer: An affirmative construction for \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) would support honest simultaneous causal-direction inference with a reproducible nonparametric nuisance procedure.

statements.statement: If Open-ended Question \(\mathrm{oeq:uniform\text{-}generated\text{-}residual\text{-}expansion}\) is resolved affirmatively for the class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), its joint event \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\), and its constant \(c_u\), there are constants \(c_\ell,c_r,C,C'>0\), depending only on the fixed envelope and kernel bandwidth, such that for the unique \(\widehat m\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), every integer \(n\), \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), and \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), with \(u_{d,\alpha}=\log(8/\alpha)+\log(2d)\), \[n\lambda\ge C\log((d+1)/\alpha)\quad\text{and}\quad r_n^4\le c_r\lambda\] imply both \(u_{d,\alpha}\le c_u n\) and \[\sup_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d(\lambda)}P^{\otimes n}(\widehat\theta_n(\widehat m)\ne\theta)\le\alpha.\] Consequently, if \(n_0=\lceil C\lambda^{-1}\log((d+1)/\alpha)\rceil\) satisfies \(n_0^{-4\beta/(2\beta+1)}\le c_r\lambda\), then \[c_\ell\frac{\log((d+1)/\alpha)}{\lambda}\le N^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)\le n_0\le C'\frac{\log((d+1)/\alpha)}{\lambda}.\] The lower bound ranges over every measurable procedure on the identical class \(\mathcal M_d(\lambda)\).
statements.justification: This is the corrected all-procedure frontier, conditional on one determinate nuisance class and its explicit simultaneous regression guarantee, with the converse proved unconditionally on the same attainable model.
statements.gap: Mooij et al. (2016) give pointwise consistency, while ordinary plug-in analysis yields only a slower nuisance-limited sufficient rate; no cited result matches upper and lower exact-recovery bounds for supplied independent ANM pairs.
statements.consumer: Practitioners receive a sample-size rule for familywise orientation of many independent scientific cause--effect modules.

statements.statement: If Open-ended Question \(\mathrm{oeq:uniform\text{-}generated\text{-}residual\text{-}expansion}\) is resolved affirmatively for \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\), and the constant \(c_u\), then for the unique \(\widehat m\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) and every \(n\) satisfying \(u_{d,\alpha}=\log(8/\alpha)+\log(2d)\le c_u n\), \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(\widehat m)\) is measurable, uses exactly \(2d\) residual-HSIC queries and \(2d\) conditional-risk queries, and satisfies \[\inf_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d(\lambda)}P^{\otimes n}\{\theta\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(\widehat m)\}\ge1-\alpha.\] For the constants \(c_r,C\) in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}minimax\text{-}frontier}\), if in addition \(n\lambda\ge C\log((d+1)/\alpha)\) and \(r_n^4\le c_r\lambda\), then \[\inf_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d(\lambda)}P^{\otimes n}\{\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(\widehat m)=\{\theta\}\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Its kernel-matrix cost is \(O(dn^2)\), and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:product\text{-}testing\text{-}converse}\) prevents uniformly honest sets from collapsing earlier by more than constants.
statements.justification: The confidence set converts the conditional rate theorem into a computable uncertainty object using the same fixed nuisance class and joint regression event, and aligns singleton output with the minimax transition.
statements.gap: Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) give asymptotically valid ordering sets through residual bootstrap, not a finite-sample uniform \(O(d)\)-query product set with a matching singleton converse.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can report every pair-orientation vector not rejected by the data instead of a single overconfident graph.

statements.statement: When \(d=1\), the confidence rule in Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\text{-}rule}\) forms \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n=B_1\) by jointly inverting both fixed-kernel residual-HSIC intervals and the cross-fitted conditional-risk intervals used in the GENE scores: a candidate \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\) is retained exactly when the interval for \(H_{1,b}\) contains \(0\), the interval for \(H_{1,-b}\) intersects \([\lambda,\infty)\), and the lower confidence bound for \(s_{1,b}-s_{1,-b}\) is nonnegative, with the defined two-direction fallback if this set is empty. The corresponding population rule selects the unique zero-HSIC direction from Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:population\text{-}direction\text{-}margin}\) while enforcing the GENE score comparison. If Open-ended Question \(\mathrm{oeq:uniform\text{-}generated\text{-}residual\text{-}expansion}\) is resolved affirmatively for \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) and \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\), and the nuisance condition in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}minimax\text{-}frontier}\) holds at its displayed \(n_0\), then \(N^*(1,\alpha,\lambda)\asymp\lambda^{-1}\log(2/\alpha)\).
statements.justification: This verifies that the \(d=1\) restriction is the bivariate joint GENE--residual-HSIC inversion actually defined by the proposal and has the intended local sample-complexity scale.
statements.gap: Mooij et al. (2016) establish consistency for this bivariate rule but not its local finite-sample sample-complexity expression.
statements.consumer: Single-pair benchmark users obtain a calibrated special case and a direct check on implementation.

sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. sample \(\mathcal W_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) from a product of \(d\) labelled bivariate laws.
sampling_model.units: Each observation contains all \(d\) supplied independent cause--effect pairs.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the orientation vector \(\theta\).
sampling_model.overlap: Each true cause and structural noise has an everywhere-positive density within one fixed Gaussian-tail envelope.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Every nuisance fit belongs to the explicitly defined class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\): deterministic balanced four-fold rotations, degree \(\lfloor\beta\rfloor\), bandwidth \(h_n\), truncation at \(T_n\), one-sided compact-boundary kernels, ridge tie-breaking, and response clipping. The open construction must jointly prove \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\) and orthogonalize fixed-Gaussian-kernel residual HSIC against exactly these fits.

estimand_functional: \(\theta_j(P)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{b\in\{-1,+1\}}H_{j,b}(P),\qquad N^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)\asymp\lambda^{-1}\log((d+1)/\alpha)\ \text{conditionally on the affirmative }\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\text{-based generated-residual expansion, }\mathcal G_n\text{, and }n_0^{-4\beta/(2\beta+1)}\le c_r\lambda\)

bibliography.citation: Li, M., Qian, H., Wang, T.-Z., Li, S., Zhang, M., and Zhou, A. (2025). Strong and weak identifiability of optimization-based causal discovery in non-linear additive noise models. Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267, 35753--35768.
Peters, J., Mooij, J. M., Janzing, D., and Schoelkopf, B. (2014). Causal discovery with continuous additive noise models. Journal of Machine Learning Research 15, 2009--2053.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: GENE adopts an order-based search framework that incorporates conditional independence tests into order fitness evaluation.
The directed acyclic graph becomes identifiable from the distribution under mild conditions.
As the main theoretical contribution of this work we prove the consistency of that method.
The asymptotic null distribution as well as the behavior of the test statistic under alternatives is investigated.
We show that our new tests are consistent against fixed alternatives, and minimax rate optimal against smooth local alternatives.
We present a general non-asymptotic framework for analyzing the minimax power of the permutation test.
We prove that the permutation test achieves the significance level and that the bootstrap test achieves pointwise asymptotic significance level.
We demonstrate the asymptotic validity of the confidence set constructed using this goodness-of-fit test.
We characterize a phase-transition phenomenon akin to the signal detection problem.
Under independence and bounded-fourth-moment kernels, martingale HSIC converges to a standard normal law.
Theorems 1.1--1.5 characterize observational--interventional sample tradeoffs for identifying the causal structure of two significantly correlated finite-domain variables.
Theorem 3.1 proves \(N_2^*(\beta,\nu,\delta)\asymp\log(1/\delta)/(d_\beta^2+\beta^2\nu^2)\) for a bivariate linear LiNGAM class.

tldr: The unconditional field headline is a feasible-image and product-minimax result for \(d\) supplied independent cause--effect pairs: after the explicit orientation permutation \(\Pi_\theta\), a positive-density restricted-ANM Hermite chart fills \([\underline g,\overline g]^d\times\{0\}^d\times[\lambda,A_H\lambda]^d\), and legal coordinate-swapped mirrors give \(N^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)\gtrsim\lambda^{-1}\log((d+1)/\alpha)\). A matching upper frontier and confidence-set singleton transition require the explicit open construction of a second-order residual-HSIC statistic for the determinate class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), jointly establishing the simultaneous \(L^4\) regression event \(\mathcal G_n\) and the dimension-correct threshold \(u=x+\log(2d)\), together with \(n\lambda\gtrsim\log((d+1)/\alpha)\) and \(r_n^4\lesssim\lambda\); the sample-size inequality also places \(u_{d,\alpha}\) inside the OEQ's permitted range.

project_justification.gap: Published ANM theory supplies qualitative direction identification and pointwise consistency, while published HSIC minimax theory treats observed variables. Acharya et al.'s discrete intervention experiment and Jin's linear-LiNGAM primitive-margin experiment do not determine the coupled GENE--residual-HSIC feasible image or the product exact-recovery boundary for nonlinear observational ANMs.
project_justification.niche: Independent supplied pairs isolate the exact geometry and product-testing difficulty without requiring a classification of arbitrary GENE landscapes.
project_justification.fill: The orientation-indexed permutation, scalar-coordinate Hermite expansions, attainable rectangle, and legal-mirror product converse form the unconditional contribution. The conditional upper result is pinned to \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), whose four-fold allocation, polynomial order, bandwidth, tail truncation, boundary correction, ridge rule, and clipping are fixed. Constructing the orthogonal statistic must jointly prove \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\) and the dimension-correct \(u=x+\log(2d)\) deviation bound before the matched frontier or singleton confidence guarantee follows; the latter claims use the same event and require \(u_{d,\alpha}\le c_u n\).

related_work: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6) and Theorem 4.3) define the relevant hybrid score and assume a global reversal ordering; this proposal is informed by their score construction but makes no claim to sharpen their theorem on arbitrary DAGs. Peters et al. (2014, Definition 27 and Theorem 28) provide the restricted positive-density identification domain used for every positive chart point. Mooij et al. (2016, Appendix A) prove pointwise consistency of regression plus fixed-kernel HSIC under a suitable learner. Acharya et al. (2023, PMLR 206, Theorems 1.1--1.5 on pages 2--3) characterize observational--interventional sample tradeoffs for two finite-alphabet variables under discrete causal-structure identification; their interventions and total-variation margin are orthogonal to the observational nonlinear residual-HSIC product experiment. Jin (2026, arXiv:2608.15840v1, Theorem 3.1 and Equation (3.13) on page 5) proves a sharp bivariate linear-LiNGAM frontier in edge-strength, source-non-Gaussianity, and scale-uncertainty margins; that primitive-margin linear experiment is orthogonal to, rather than a substitute for, the nonlinear fixed-kernel residual-HSIC geometry here. Hl\'avka, Hu\v{s}kov\'a, and Meintanis (2011) show that estimated residuals require their own nuisance expansion; the open claim here is restricted to the fully specified four-fold class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), including its simultaneous \(L^4\) guarantee, rather than an unspecified suitable learner. Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (2023, Theorems 6, 7, and 10) and Kim, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman (2022, Sections 3--7) provide observed-variable testing constructions and minimax templates. Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) justify asymptotic residual ordering and sample splitting without the local uniform rate needed here. Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026, JASA 121(553), 690--703, Sections 2--4) motivate inversion into causal-order confidence sets, while Gao and Stoev (2020) motivate the distinction between coordinatewise and exact simultaneous recovery. The 2026 martingale-HSIC preprint is adjacent calibration work for observed variables and is treated only as methodological context. Wornbard et al. receive non-archival credit for the presolve insight; no public theorem text under that attribution was locatable, so it is not used as a comparator.
technical_internal_limitation: The proposed \(\lambda^{-1}\) upper frontier is not licensed by ordinary sample splitting or by merely postulating a suitable learner. The open construction is restricted to \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) and must prove the joint event \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\) for its fixed degree, bandwidth, truncation, boundary, clipping, and four-fold rules. It must then cancel both the first derivative and the diagonal second-order bias uniformly, turn the event's \(L^4\) error into the displayed \(r_n^4\) remainder, and pay for all \(2d\) queries through \(u=x+\log(2d)\). Failure of either the regression guarantee or the orthogonal expansion under the fixed envelope would preserve the attainable rectangle and product converse but force a slower or narrower upper frontier.
honest_scope: The orientation-permuted attainable rectangle, mirror-information proposition, and product-testing converse are unconditional theorem targets and form the field headline. The genuinely open construction is the joint generated-residual result for the determinate class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\): it must establish \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\) and the residual-HSIC expansion with simultaneous \(u=x+\log(2d)\). The matching upper minimax bound requires that construction and the inequalities \(n\lambda\ge C\log((d+1)/\alpha)\) and \(r_n^4\le c_r\lambda\); the confidence-set coverage also requires \(u_{d,\alpha}\le c_u n\), and its singleton guarantee is conditional on exactly the same class, event, and signal inequalities. Acharya et al.'s discrete intervention model and Jin's linear LiNGAM model are distinct experiments, not competing answers to this nonlinear residual-HSIC question. At \(d=1\), the population rule reduces to the familiar bivariate regression--HSIC direction choice; the new content is its local margin geometry and conditional uniform rate, not a new qualitative identification rule.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Characterize the feasible set of joint GENE correcting gains and fixed-Gaussian-kernel residual-HSIC margins inside one positive-density restricted additive-noise envelope.
seed_details.summary: Perturb a reversible standardized Gaussian pair by a quadratic Hermite mechanism and prove that the GENE gain remains in an interior interval while the wrong-direction HSIC fills an interval of order \(t^2\); tensorization then gives a \(2d\)-dimensional scaled rectangle in \(\mathfrak F_d\).
seed_details.anchor_read: Li et al., Section 4.1, Equation (6), and Theorem 4.3 define the hybrid fitness and assume a global reversal ordering; their proof on page 14 is combinatorial once that ordering is imposed. Their conclusion discusses pruning and other structural models, not attainable quantitative margins. Peters et al., Definition 27 and Theorem 28, supplies the restricted-ANM legality check for every nonzero perturbation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Li et al.'s assumed comparison of two order fitness values by a one-sided local expansion of the population correlation ratio and reverse-residual HSIC around the reversible Gaussian boundary.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the pair \(\{\text{restricted ANM margin geometry},\text{fixed-kernel HSIC}\}\) located identifiability and testing papers but no theorem describing the joint attainable image.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Peters et al. because restricted ANMs already identify the direction.
seed_details.rebuttal: Peters et al. prove qualitative uniqueness and do not control either coordinate of the GENE--HSIC margin map near the reversible boundary.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine the all-procedure minimax sample complexity for simultaneously orienting \(d\) supplied independent restricted-ANM pairs over an attainable product class.
seed_details.summary: Prove the unconditional lower bound \(N^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)\gtrsim\lambda^{-1}\log((d+1)/\alpha)\) on the attainable class using tensorized mirror experiments, and obtain the matching implementable upper bound only if the fixed class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) satisfies the joint regression and generated-residual expansion with \(r_n^4\lesssim\lambda\).
seed_details.anchor_read: Mooij et al., Appendix A, Theorem 20 and the consistency theorem following it compare fitted-residual HSIC in both directions under a suitable learner. Section 6 explicitly limits the empirical claim to the benchmark evidence; there is no uniform finite-sample or simultaneous minimax statement.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: For the fully specified four-fold local-polynomial class, prove the simultaneous \(L^4\) regression event and then a uniform exponential oracle-to-fitted expansion at the local scale \(n\lambda\), before applying the simultaneous union bound.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining simultaneous exact orientation, generated residuals, and minimax HSIC found single observed-variable tests, Acharya et al.'s discrete intervention experiment, Jin's bivariate linear-LiNGAM experiment, and strong-classification analogies, but no nonlinear residual-HSIC product-ANM frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from applying a union bound to a minimax-optimal HSIC test and an Assouad lower bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: Existing tests observe both tested variables; here one variable is a learned residual, and the hard alternatives must remain identifiable restricted ANMs while realizing the same margin geometry.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Construct a cross-fitted fixed-Gaussian-kernel residual-HSIC procedure whose regression-nuisance perturbation is negligible at the simultaneous local-power scale.
seed_details.summary: For the deterministic class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), jointly prove its simultaneous \(L^4\) regression event, orthogonalize the residual kernel mean embedding before cross multiplication, and derive a uniform moderate-deviation expansion with fourth-order regression remainder.
seed_details.anchor_read: Hl\'avka, Hu\v{s}kov\'a, and Meintanis construct tests from characteristic functions of estimated residuals and separately analyze their null law and alternatives. Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas, Theorems 6, 7, and 10, obtain studentized cross-HSIC limits and local power only when the tested variables are observed.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Establish the foldwise \(L^4\) guarantee for the fixed truncated boundary-corrected local-polynomial protocol, then insert a Gateaux-derivative projection into the centered kernel feature map before the cross-U-statistic is formed.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for orthogonalized HSIC with generated regression residuals found sample-splitting validity and observed-variable martingale or cross-HSIC, but no uniform fourth-order nuisance remainder for ANM orientation.
seed_details.red_team: Cross-fitting alone already removes regression overfitting bias.
seed_details.rebuttal: Cross-fitting restores conditional independence between training and evaluation folds but does not cancel the first nonzero functional derivative of HSIC with respect to the learned regression.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine an efficiency bound for ANM orientation under a fixed smooth envelope.
seed_details.summary: Embed the discrete direction in a regular local asymmetry path and characterize the efficient score for its signed local parameter.
seed_details.anchor_read: Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas derive Gaussian null limits and minimax local power, not a semiparametric influence function for a causal direction parameter.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace their composite independence null by a differentiable signed asymmetry parameter through the reversible boundary.
seed_details.destination_search: The named search obstruction is nonregularity: the orientation itself is discrete and undefined at the reversible boundary, so an efficiency bound depends on an arbitrary path parameter rather than the stated causal target.
seed_details.red_team: The efficiency object is a path-dependent surrogate for a nonregular binary target.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the present question, so the seed is dropped rather than promoted as an efficiency result.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Construct a measurable \(O(d)\)-query confidence set for all supplied pair orientations with a sharp singleton transition.
seed_details.summary: Invert pairwise residual-independence tests over the deterministic orientation cube, using a fallback rule that preserves coverage when neither candidate passes.
seed_details.anchor_read: Wang, Kolar, and Drton, Sections 2--4, invert residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests over orderings and prove asymptotic coverage. Their conclusion emphasizes ancestral and effect uncertainty, but does not give a finite-sample product-pair singleton boundary.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace global order enumeration and bootstrap calibration by a deterministic \(2d\)-query product inversion with one simultaneous critical value.
seed_details.destination_search: Permutation and conformal searches found exact symmetry tests for observed quantities, but fitted residuals are not exchangeable under naive permutations; the confidence-set object survives, while exact permutation coverage does not.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely Bonferroni inversion of \(d\) familiar tests.
seed_details.rebuttal: The set construction is routine after valid local tests exist, so it is retained only as a consumer theorem and not as the independent kernel.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Assess whether pairwise orientation can be formulated as a statistical treatment-choice problem.
seed_details.summary: Choose which orientations to report under abstention costs and compare to an oracle decision rule.
seed_details.anchor_read: Gao and Stoev study exact versus approximate support recovery and supply a strong-classification analogy, not a causal welfare functional or deployable treatment rule.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Introduce an abstention loss in place of exact graph recovery.
seed_details.destination_search: The named obstruction is substantive rather than technical: no treatment, welfare, or policy-value functional exists in the supplied-pair problem, so M16 would change the scientific target.
seed_details.red_team: The policy is an artificial relabeling of a graph estimator.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, so the M16 lane is documented and dropped.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Allocate a fixed observation budget adaptively across supplied independent cause--effect pairs.
seed_details.summary: Derive an instance-dependent allocation frontier when pair-specific residual-HSIC margins differ.
seed_details.anchor_read: Kim, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman, Sections 3--7, use moment and exponential concentration arguments for minimax permutation tests; their discussion does not consider sequential allocation across separate experiments.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a common sample size by stopping times indexed by pair-specific confidence sequences.
seed_details.destination_search: Sequential kernel-independence testing exists for observed pairs, but the current data arrive as joint observations of all supplied pairs, leaving no meaningful allocation decision without changing the sampling design.
seed_details.red_team: Adaptive allocation is unavailable because each draw observes every pair simultaneously.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds under the stated sampling model, so the seed is dropped.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Separate the exact simultaneous orientation boundary from the average Hamming-risk boundary.
seed_details.summary: Prove that average coordinate risk needs order \(\lambda^{-1}\log(1/\alpha)\), whereas exact recovery needs the additional \(\lambda^{-1}\log d\) term on the same mirror family.
seed_details.anchor_read: Gao and Stoev distinguish strong classification from weaker coordinatewise criteria through maxima and multiple-testing boundaries. Their model is sparse-signal support recovery rather than ANM orientation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Transport the coordinatewise likelihood-ratio calculation to legal opposite-orientation ANM mirror pairs.
seed_details.destination_search: No located causal-direction paper derives both losses on one attainable ANM class.
seed_details.red_team: The loss separation is a routine consequence once the product converse is proved.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is substantially correct, so this becomes a corollary-level diagnostic rather than the proposal kernel.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine whether martingale HSIC or cross-HSIC is preferable for simultaneous generated-residual testing.
seed_details.summary: Derive a nuisance-rate frontier on which martingale and cross statistics have the same local power and a regime where one loses calibration.
seed_details.anchor_read: Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas construct cross-HSIC by splitting and studentizing two cross-covariance estimates. The 2026 public preprint on martingale HSIC replaces rectangular cross blocks by a lower-triangular self-normalized sum for observed variables.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition the martingale increments on a regression-training fold and propagate the learned-residual error through the conditional centering identity.
seed_details.destination_search: The observed-variable comparison is occupied, but no generated-residual frontier was located; nevertheless, it is secondary to establishing any uniformly valid residual statistic.
seed_details.red_team: A comparator frontier is premature before the nuisance expansion is known to exist.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection limits feasibility, so the seed is deferred behind the orthogonal-residual question.

literature_map.anchor: Li et al., Section 4.1 and Equation (6), define GENE's scale-normalized regression fitness with residual-independence penalties; Theorem 4.3 assumes global reversal monotonicity, and its page-14 proof is combinatorial conditional on that assumption. Peters et al., Definition 27 and Theorem 28, identify positive-density restricted ANMs but supply no quantitative margin geometry.
adjacent_threads: Mooij et al., Appendix A, prove pointwise consistency of fixed-kernel data-split ANM-HSIC under a suitable regression learner; the proof uses convergence, not a uniform local-power remainder.

Hl\'avka, Hu\v{s}kov\'a, and Meintanis analyze independence statistics formed from estimated nonparametric-regression residuals and establish that nuisance estimation needs its own expansion; they do not provide the simultaneous \(L^4\) guarantee for the fixed class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\).

Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas, Theorems 6, 7, and 10, provide observed-variable cross-HSIC null limits and minimax local power; Kim, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman provide the nonasymptotic permutation-test concentration and minimax template.
Pfister et al., Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3, show asymptotic ordering and sample-splitting validity for estimated residuals, but do not give a uniform local margin bound.
Wang, Kolar, and Drton invert residual-bootstrap tests into asymptotically valid ordering confidence sets; Gao and Stoev provide the strong-classification analogy for the logarithmic dimension term.

Acharya et al. (2023), PMLR 206, Theorems 1.1--1.5 on pages 2--3, give tight regimes for the observational--interventional sample tradeoff in two-variable finite-alphabet causal-structure identification. Their intervention access and discrete total-variation separation are orthogonal to the observational nonlinear residual-HSIC product experiment.

Jin (2026), arXiv:2608.15840v1, Theorem 3.1 and Equation (3.13) on page 5, gives a sharp bivariate linear-LiNGAM direction law in edge strength, source non-Gaussianity, and scale uncertainty. Those linear primitive margins do not replace the fixed-kernel reverse-residual-HSIC margin or the \(d\)-pair product geometry here.

The 2026 public preprint on martingale HSIC gives observed-variable normal calibration without permutations, but does not analyze nonparametrically generated ANM residuals. No closer paper located in the target--method search subsumes the proposed attainable rectangle or uniform product frontier.

candidate_scans.settled_boundary: Restricted-ANM uniqueness and the definition of population HSIC are settled; the first changed step is the joint local expansion of GENE gain and reverse-residual HSIC.
candidate_scans.occupancy: No located paper gives a box-inclusion or Jacobian theorem for the image \(\mathfrak F_d\).

candidate_scans.settled_boundary: Single observed-variable testing rates, discrete causal-structure testing with interventions, bivariate linear-LiNGAM minimax rates, and noncausal strong-classification lower bounds are settled in their own models; a uniform result for the explicit class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) is not.
candidate_scans.occupancy: No located result proves the attainable nonlinear residual-HSIC rectangle or the \(d\)-pair legal-mirror lower bound on one positive-density restricted-ANM product class.

candidate_scans.settled_boundary: Pointwise fitted-residual validity and observed-variable studentization are settled; uniform oracle-to-fitted equivalence at \(n\lambda\) scale is not.
candidate_scans.occupancy: The search found no joint simultaneous \(L^4\) regression guarantee and second-order orthogonal residual-embedding construction with a fourth-order remainder for the fixed four-fold truncated local-polynomial protocol.

literature_map.settled: Qualitative restricted-ANM direction identification, pointwise consistency of regression-plus-HSIC orientation, observed-variable HSIC testing, discrete intervention-assisted two-variable testing, sharp bivariate linear-LiNGAM minimax testing, and asymptotic inversion into causal-order confidence sets are settled in the cited settings.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: The exact pair \(\{\text{attainable nonlinear GENE--HSIC margin geometry},\text{product exact recovery over generated residuals}\}\) is unoccupied in the located literature; the Acharya et al. intervention/discrete-CSI and Jin linear-LiNGAM experiments are orthogonal comparators.
